Four control values. One easing curve. x is time; y is progress, which can fall below 0% or exceed 100%. The output is a timing-function only, not a duration.

Leaving or changing language does not retain inputs. Reloading restores the defaults.

03 / Take the CSS

You can also select text in the read-only field and copy manually. The output does not include a duration.

An already-started system copy may finish. Editing or leaving only cancels this page’s success message; it does not clear the system clipboard.

Reading the curve

Why can progress exceed 100%?

The y controls range from −1 to 2, so a curve may move backward or overshoot before returning to the end. This is not a physical spring simulation.

Can x1 be greater than x2?

Yes. Both x values must lie between 0 and 1. The tool uses exact bisection to invert time; it never swaps your control points.

Where do my inputs go?

Calculation stays in this page. Inputs are not stored, uploaded or put in the URL. There is no analytics. Copy writes only after an explicit click and never reads the clipboard.
